graph.title: Graph a gear ratio
graph.prompt: A gear turns the wheel three times per pedal turn. Choose the horizontal quantity, plot the readings for one and two pedal turns, then describe the relationship.
graph.criterion: Choose the input axis, plot both ordered pairs, and express the direction of dependence.
graph.hint: Use the input as x. Each step along x adds three wheel turns.

fields.label: Relationship in words
fields.key: The wheel makes three turns per pedal turn.
choices: The wheel makes three turns per pedal turn.
The pedal makes three turns per wheel turn.

axes.title: Choose the input axis
axes.prompt: A cyclist controls the pedal turns and observes wheel turns. Label the horizontal input and vertical output.
axes.criterion: Distinguish the controlled and dependent quantities.
axes.hint: Which quantity does the cyclist change first?

words.title: Explain the ratio in words
words.prompt: Your points show (1,3) and (2,6). When pedal turns double, what happens to wheel turns, and why?
words.criterion: Explain how doubling the input doubles the output while the ratio stays constant.
words.hint: Compare the change from three wheel turns to six with the change from one pedal turn to two.

fields.label: Explain the change
choices: Wheel turns double because each pedal turn still gives three wheel turns.
Wheel turns stay at three because the ratio stays at three.
fields.key: Wheel turns double because each pedal turn still gives three wheel turns.

graph-transfer.title: Graph a changed ratio
graph-transfer.prompt: A new gear produces two wheel turns per pedal turn. Choose the horizontal quantity and plot three and four pedal turns.
graph-transfer.criterion: Independently translate a changed ratio into coordinates.
graph-transfer.hint: Multiply the pedal turns by two to find wheel turns.

table.title: Build a ratio table
table.prompt: A gear produces four wheel turns per pedal turn. Fill the output column for each input.
table.criterion: Preserve the same factor across the table.

order.title: Order a fair comparison
order.prompt: Arrange the steps of a fair comparison of two paper planes. Choose the action for each position.
order.criterion: Set controls before observing either flight and compare only after measuring both.
order.hint: Begin by fixing the launch conditions.

repair.title: Repair a formula
repair.prompt: A sheet records pedal turns in A2 and wheel turns in B2. Each pedal turn produces three wheel turns. B2 currently uses =A2/3. Locate the error and test your repair with A2 = 4.
repair.criterion: Locate the operation error and check the corrected result.
repair.hint: The output is larger than the input.

case.title: Decide what the evidence supports
case.prompt: A station log records one late train. A passenger says trains are always late. Which claim can this evidence support? Explain what further evidence would test the broader claim.
case.criterion: Choose the bounded claim and propose sampling multiple scheduled arrivals.
case.hint: Separate the single recorded observation from a claim about many days.

case-update.title: Reconsider a claim
case-update.prompt: A month of complete records shows 18 late trains in 100 arrivals. Revise your claim and explain which evidence changed it.
case-update.criterion: State the observed proportion and restrict the conclusion to the recorded month.
case-update.hint: Compare late arrivals with all arrivals in the same period.

revise.title: Write a public notice
revise.prompt: The east entrance closes Monday. The west entrance stays open. Draft a one-sentence notice for first-time visitors.
revise.criterion: Tell the reader when the closure occurs and which entrance to use.
revise.hint: Picture what a visitor needs to do on arrival.

revision.title: Revise a notice
revision.prompt: The west entrance has steps. The level entrance is on Oak Street. Revise your original notice so someone using a wheelchair can act on it.
revision.criterion: Retain the closure time and give an actionable level-access route.
revision.hint: Name the street and identify the level entrance.

experiment.title: Predict before a flight
experiment.prompt: Two simulated planes launch at the same speed. Predict which travels farther with a longer wing in this model and choose a variable to keep fixed. The measured distances appear after you commit your prediction.
experiment.criterion: Make a prediction before observing the result and control launch speed.
experiment.hint: Vary one feature at a time.

measure.title: Interpret a simulation
measure.prompt: In this model, distance in metres is wing length in cm × 0.4 at constant launch speed. Try two wing lengths, run the model, and explain how the observations bear on your saved prediction.
measure.criterion: Use two distinct positive wing lengths, the resulting distances, and the prior prediction to explain the modeled relationship.
measure.hint: Compare the measured change in distance to the change in length.

perform.title: Perform a steady pulse
perform.prompt: Tap four beats at roughly one beat per second using the tap control or F6 in the terminal. Describe any other practice separately.
perform.criterion: Measure three intervals between direct taps. A description alone supplies self-report.
perform.hint: Count evenly before starting the first tap.

retrieve.title: Reconstruct a unit rate
retrieve.prompt: From memory, a pump moves 18 litres in 3 minutes. Give its rate in litres per minute.
retrieve.criterion: Reconstruct a unit rate without a cue.
retrieve.hint: Divide total litres by elapsed minutes.

transfer.title: Transfer a unit rate
transfer.prompt: A printer produces 28 pages in 4 minutes. At the same rate, how many pages will it produce in 9 minutes?
transfer.criterion: Use a unit rate under changed conditions.
transfer.hint: First find pages printed in one minute.

annotate.title: Annotate a source
annotate.prompt: Bring a short plain-text source. Select one sentence, quote it exactly, and explain what claim the sentence supports and what remains uncertain.
annotate.criterion: Ground the claim in the quoted source and identify a limit to the evidence.
annotate.hint: Look for a sentence you could point to if someone asked how you know.
